miniProject.title: Fenced shard movement and recoverable transaction workflows
miniProject.brief: Extend `loglab` from a replicated group to versioned shard ownership and durable cross-shard work on your machine. Build reduced isolation, atomic-commit and saga fixtures over the existing log, comparing their guarantees and recovery costs without treating compensation as rollback or routing versions as revocation.
steps: Build `shard/` placement for range, hash, weighted virtual-node rings and rendezvous routing. Compare joins, leaves and scans with exhaustive placement and access-pattern oracles; retain key/byte movement and fan-out predictions. Check replica placement against independently enumerated failure-domain losses rather than counting virtual nodes as independent replicas.

Implement atomic versioned maps, refresh-and-retry routing and fenced freeze/install/delete movement while unaffected shards serve. Check ownership and retained writes against a sequential oracle across stale routes, delayed migration RPCs and controller restart from durable current/next configurations; retain traces. Optionally run MIT 6.5840 Lab 5A/5B.

Build shared/exclusive locking with growing/shrinking phases, commit-held locks, predicate protection and wait-for-cycle aborts in `txn/`. Check anomaly fixtures against Berenson's definitions and transaction results against independent serial-order enumeration, including real-time constraints; retain deadlock, phantom, retry and serializable-but-not-strictly-serializable regressions.

Add MVCC version selection, safe reclamation and shared-timestamp reads across shards, waiting for each safe time including unresolved prepares. Check against a version-history oracle; retain pinned-snapshot and lagging-shard regressions. Compare per-shard/global index queries and CDC-fed updates with full scans, preserving postings/fetch/merge costs and staleness evidence.

Implement durable prepare, tentative writes, lock recovery and coordinator decisions using the Building Distributed Systems two-phase-commit and coordinator-failure drills as protocol checks. Restart at each persistence boundary and duplicate decisions; compare recovered results with an independent atomic-outcome oracle, preserving in-doubt blocking and timeout-after-commit histories.

Build `txn/`'s durable saga with outbox/inbox transactions, ordered relaying and atomic processed-ID/effect storage. Inject coordinator death, ambiguous replies, duplicates and failed compensation; compare paused per-business ledgers with independent invariants. Retain fenced recovery, bounded retries/escalation, irreversible-pivot policy and pending-versus-terminal verdicts.

After deterministic gates, run repeated matched baseline/fault comparisons, validating extraction against hand-counted histories. Retain versions, workloads, latency distributions, skew, hot-key split/read-fan-out, scatter-gather tails, moved keys/bytes, cutover availability, abort/compensation denominators, suppressed deliveries versus duplicate effects, goodput, recovery predicates and invariant verdicts; include unresolved and negative regimes.
deliverables: The `shard/` routing and recoverable movement fixture plus `txn/` isolation, atomic-commit, saga, outbox and inbox implementations.
Independent placement, version-history, serial-order and business-ledger checks with deterministic crash, stale-owner, deadlock and compensation regressions in `tests/` and `faults/`.
Raw histories and repeated matched cost reports in `reports/`, with explicit atomic boundaries, irreversible steps, pending work and recovery assumptions.

checks.name: MIT 6.5840 Spring 2026 Lab 5 Sharded KV, Parts A and B
checks.note: Optional after working Labs 2 through 4; retain movement and controller-recovery results. Your durable movement fixture remains required; keep course solutions private.

checks.name: Building Distributed Systems: two-phase commit and coordinator failure, TW-1 and TW-2
checks.note: Use the browser-graded protocol drills; retain your own durable restart and duplicate-decision evidence beyond their exchange and logging checks.

rubric.pass: Your placement oracle checks movement and failure-domain survival; sequential-model tests preserve acknowledged writes and exclusive serving authority across stale routes, movement crashes and controller recovery.
rubric.strong: Interrupted transitions resume without silent drops; per-event evidence distinguishes map publication, source fencing and destination activation while unaffected shards continue serving.

rubric.pass: Your independent serial-order and version-history oracles validate locking and snapshot fixtures. Atomic-outcome checks cover durable prepare, decisions, recovered locks and duplicate decisions without treating timeout as abort permission.
rubric.strong: Negative controls expose phantoms, write skew, premature version reclamation and inconsistent shard snapshots; recovery evidence explains permitted blocking separately from isolation or atomicity violations.

rubric.pass: Your paused per-business ledger oracle catches false terminal status and duplicate effects; outbox/inbox recovery handles ambiguous replies and failed compensation. Hand-counted metrics validate repeated matched runs with named versions and workloads.
rubric.strong: Reconciliation preserves unresolved irreversible effects and retry escalation; measured skew, movement, tails, aborts and recovery costs retain negative regimes without weakening invariants or hiding pending work.

miniProject.feedsInto: Fenced ownership, recoverable transactions and outbox/inbox boundaries feed partition logs, consumer reassignment, CDC and stream checkpoints. Independent reconciliation, crash histories and matched cost evidence support the capstone's transaction and recovery defense.
